change: Engine media repair: unreferenced LFS-pointer fixture, and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE support

problem1.what: packages/producer/tests/hdr-regression/src/hdr-photo-pq.png is a 129-byte Git LFS pointer, not PNG data.
problem1.verifiedIndependently: Read the file: 'version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1', oid sha256 ba30a9ccd79bd7f283c9d3d7ec273513e95dc45bf3b9660c0a4f8463d6b523fa, size 3026. The PNG parsers were correctly rejecting pointer text.
problem1.recoveryAttempted: The real 3026-byte object is NOT recoverable locally. .git/lfs holds zero objects, and the frozen provenance baseline at _sources/hyperframes-main/... contains the SAME 129-byte pointer (sha256 3b88d391262a2bdf845a01c9cdd74ae2c99ae726c56ef5f66f46da879b64ecf2). The photograph was never imported, so an engine-owned fixture is the only option here.
problem1.fix: Engine tests now use packages/engine/src/utils/fixtures/hdr-pq-metadata.png - a real 110-byte RGB16/PQ PNG (signature 89 50 4e 47, sha256 a378739e60368f245e7f046cabe38e9cd9399ab883a9b2973be57af88fb3c665), with a fixture-local .gitattributes so it cannot become another pointer.
problem1.scope: The producer photograph is untouched and is NOT recovered. After this change no .ts/.mjs/.json under packages/ references hdr-photo-pq by name.

problem2.what: Both audio readers rejected WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (0xfffe / 65534), which FFmpeg 5.1 writes for sample widths above 16 bits, including pcm_f32le.
problem2.symptom: AudioFxRenderError: Unsupported WAV format 65534/32-bit; the envelope baker returned false.
problem2.fix: packages/engine/src/services/wavFormat.ts parses the extension properly: it requires a complete fmt chunk (size >= 40), a bounded cbSize (>= 22 and within the chunk), wValidBitsPerSample equal to the container width, and a full 16-byte subtype GUID compared byte-for-byte against KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_PCM / IEEE_FLOAT. Unknown GUIDs, truncated extensions and unsupported widths stay rejected. It does not infer float from a partial GUID match.
problem2.reviewNote: I checked the little-endian subtype constants by hand against the documented GUIDs; both are correct.
